stimulus.text: Emperor penguins breed on Antarctic ice during the coldest months of the year. To survive winds that can strip away body heat, thousands of birds pack themselves into a ______ mass, each individual sheltering against its neighbors. Birds on the group's cold outer edge slowly shuffle toward the center, while those that had been sheltered take a turn on the perimeter, so that the huddle rotates and no single penguin is left exposed for long.

items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

options.A: scattered
options.B: fragile
options.C: compact
options.D: transparent

items.rationale: The surrounding text describes birds packing tightly together and rotating so no one stays on the exposed edge, which matches 'compact,' a mass with little space between individuals.

A.explanation: Scattered means spread apart, the opposite of penguins pressing together into one mass as the text describes.

B.explanation: Fragile suggests something easily broken or weak, not the dense, sturdy grouping the text describes as protection from wind.

D.explanation: Transparent concerns seeing through something, an idea about clarity or visibility that the passage never raises.

items.topic: Fiction: a child learning to swim in a lake

stimulus.attribution: Adapted from Inés Duarte's story "Past the Shallow Edge" (fictional)
stimulus.text: Tomasz waded in only to his knees, the cold lake water pulling goosebumps up his arms. His older cousin swam a slow circle nearby, calling out that the water only felt warm once you were in past your shoulders. Tomasz didn't quite believe her, but he was tired of standing at the shallow edge while everyone else glided past him, so he took a breath and ______ himself forward into water deep enough to swim in.

items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

options.A: launched
options.B: apologized
options.C: wandered
options.D: retreated

items.rationale: The passage shows Tomasz overcoming hesitation with a decisive, forward motion ('took a breath') into deeper water, which matches 'launched.'

B.explanation: Nothing in the passage suggests Tomasz says sorry to anyone; the sentence concerns physical motion into the water, not speech.

C.explanation: Wandered implies aimless, undirected movement, but Tomasz's motion is purposeful and sudden, following a deliberate breath.

D.explanation: Retreated means moving backward, but the sentence specifies he moved 'forward into water deep enough to swim in.'

items.topic: The abacus as a calculating tool

stimulus.text: Long before mechanical calculators appeared, merchants across Asia and the Mediterranean relied on the abacus, a frame of sliding beads, to keep pace with rapid trade. A skilled user could ______ figures for a large transaction almost as quickly as a modern clerk taps them into a device, moving beads in practiced patterns that translated directly into sums, differences, and running totals.

items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

options.A: memorize
options.B: estimate
options.C: tally
options.D: invent

items.rationale: The passage describes exact 'sums, differences, and running totals,' which matches 'tally,' meaning to add up figures precisely, not approximate or invent them.

A.explanation: The passage is about calculating totals with beads, not about committing numbers to memory.

B.explanation: Estimate implies an approximate result, but the passage emphasizes precise sums and running totals, not rough guesses.

D.explanation: Invent means to create something new, which does not fit a sentence about processing existing transaction figures.

stimulus.title: Night Market
stimulus.text:
Lanterns unstitch the dark seam by seam,
oil hissing where the flatbread blisters,
a vendor calling the price of mangoes
in three languages before the coins are cold.
{u}Somewhere under all that noise, an old woman counts stitches into a sock, waiting for no customer at all.{/u}
The market does not pause for her patience;
it moves like a river around a stone,
loud on every side of her stillness.

items.stem: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?

options.A: It introduces a figure of stillness that contrasts with the market's motion and noise, a contrast the closing lines develop.
options.B: It suggests that the woman's goods are too expensive for most customers to afford.
options.C: It shifts the setting from the market to the woman's home for the remainder of the poem.
options.D: It resolves the contrast between noise and calm that the poem has built toward.

items.rationale: The underlined sentence sets the old woman's quiet, unhurried mending against the surrounding market's bustle; the final lines ('loud on every side of her stillness') extend exactly this contrast.

B.explanation: The poem never mentions prices for the woman's goods or their affordability; it only notes she is 'waiting for no customer at all.'

C.explanation: The poem stays in the market; the line right after the underlined sentence states 'the market does not pause for her,' confirming the setting has not changed.

D.explanation: The sentence introduces the contrast between noise and stillness; the poem continues describing that contrast rather than resolving it.

items.topic: Salt flats and why they are so level

stimulus.text: Salt flats that form in enclosed desert basins can stretch for many kilometers with a surface so flat that elevation varies by only a few centimeters from edge to edge. Seasonal floods spread a thin sheet of water evenly across the basin; as that water evaporates, it deposits a fresh layer of dissolved minerals across the entire surface rather than piling minerals into mounds. {u}Over centuries, repeated flooding and evaporation smooth out any low spots and gradually wear down any high spots as well.{/u} The result is one of the flattest natural surfaces on Earth.

items.stem: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?

options.A: It explains the repeated natural process that produces the extreme flatness described earlier in the text.
options.B: It gives one example among several types of desert basins discussed in the text.
options.C: It contradicts the passage's claim that salt flats are extremely flat.
options.D: It shifts the focus from how salt flats form to how travelers use them.

items.rationale: The sentence describes the cycle of flooding and evaporation that levels high and low spots, directly explaining the mechanism behind the extreme flatness the passage opens and closes with.

B.explanation: The text discusses one process in one kind of basin, not multiple types of desert basins being compared.

C.explanation: The sentence supports the claim of extreme flatness by explaining how it forms; it does not contradict it.

D.explanation: The passage never discusses how people use salt flats; it stays focused on their formation.

items.topic: Homework and learning: two fictional education researchers

stimulus.text1: Education researcher Petra Lindqvist argues that short, regular homework assignments help students consolidate what they learned in class that same day. In her studies of secondary school students, those who completed brief nightly review exercises scored higher on unit tests than students who received identical classroom instruction but did no additional practice at home.
stimulus.text2: Education researcher Amara Osei contends that homework's apparent benefits often reflect which students already study effectively rather than what homework itself teaches. In her surveys, students who already reviewed their notes independently kept doing so whether or not homework was assigned, while students who did not already study rarely completed homework consistently enough for it to change their results.

items.stem: Which choice best describes a difference in how Lindqvist and Osei interpret evidence that homework correlates with higher test scores?

options.A: Both researchers agree that homework causes the improvement, but they disagree about how much homework is optimal.
options.B: Lindqvist attributes the correlation to students' independent study habits, while Osei attributes it to homework itself.
options.C: Osei argues that homework should be replaced entirely by extra classroom instruction, a position Lindqvist rejects.
options.D: Lindqvist treats the correlation as evidence that homework causes the improvement, while Osei attributes it mainly to differences in students' independent study habits.

items.rationale: Lindqvist's studies compare identical instruction with and without homework and credit homework for the score gain, while Osei's surveys trace the same correlation to study habits that exist with or without homework being assigned.

A.explanation: Osei explicitly doubts that homework itself causes the improvement, so the two researchers do not agree on causation.

B.explanation: This reverses the two positions: it is Osei, not Lindqvist, who attributes the correlation to study habits.

C.explanation: Osei questions whether homework causes score gains but never proposes eliminating homework or replacing it with more classroom instruction.

items.topic: Why zebras have stripes: two hypotheses

stimulus.text1: Biologist Dana Kowalczyk argues that a zebra's stripes evolved primarily to reduce bites from blood-feeding flies. She points to experiments in which horses fitted with striped coverings were landed on far less often by flies than horses in solid-colored coverings, and she suggests the contrast between light and dark bands disrupts the polarized light patterns flies use to find a landing surface.
stimulus.text2: Biologist Femi Adeyemi maintains that stripes primarily help zebras avoid detection by predators moving through tall, sunlit grass, where alternating light and dark bands break up the animal's outline. He notes that fly-landing experiments have also found reduced landings on animals wearing several other high-contrast patterns, not stripes alone, which he says weakens any claim that stripe pattern specifically explains the effect.

items.stem: Which choice best describes a difference in how Kowalczyk and Adeyemi would most likely interpret a new finding that fly landings decrease on any animal covering with strong light-dark contrast, regardless of its pattern?

options.A: Kowalczyk would reject the finding outright, while Adeyemi would use it to argue that predator avoidance, not flies, drives stripe evolution.
options.B: Both researchers would treat the finding as unrelated to their hypotheses, since it concerns contrast rather than stripes specifically.
options.C: Adeyemi would see the finding as undermining his own hypothesis about predator avoidance.
options.D: Kowalczyk would likely see the finding as support for her hypothesis only if the contrast resembles stripe width specifically, while Adeyemi would treat it as confirming his doubt that stripes uniquely explain reduced fly landings.

items.rationale: Kowalczyk's argument depends on stripe width disrupting light patterns, so a pattern-general effect would support her view only if it resembled that mechanism; Adeyemi already cites this exact kind of finding as evidence against a stripe-specific explanation.

A.explanation: Nothing suggests Kowalczyk would reject the finding outright rather than qualify her claim, and the passage does not say Adeyemi would use it to argue for predator avoidance specifically.

B.explanation: The finding is directly related to both hypotheses, especially Adeyemi's point that contrast-based effects extend beyond stripes.

C.explanation: Adeyemi's hypothesis concerns predator avoidance, not fly landings, so a finding about fly landings and contrast would not undermine his own hypothesis; it undermines the rival fly hypothesis instead.

items.topic: Fiction: a gardener before a storm

stimulus.attribution: Adapted from Yusuf Bello's story "The Greenish Sky" (fictional)
stimulus.text: Before the first thunderclap sounded, Old Ren went out to stake down his tomato plants. He had lived by the coast long enough to read the sky: a greenish tint over the western hills, gulls flying inland instead of out to sea, the sudden hush of insects that usually sang from the hedges. He worked quickly, tying twine to each fragile stem, because he knew that the plants he had tended all spring could be flattened in minutes once the wind arrived.

items.stem: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?

options.A: Ren has never experienced a storm this severe and is uncertain how to prepare.
options.B: Ren recognizes signs of an approaching storm and hurries to protect his garden before it strikes.
options.C: Ren mainly wants to understand why gulls fly inland before storms.
options.D: Ren believes his garden cannot survive any strong wind no matter how well he prepares.

items.rationale: The passage centers on Ren reading storm signs and quickly staking his plants to protect them before the wind arrives, which is the main action and idea of the passage.

A.explanation: The passage says Ren 'had lived by the coast long enough to read the sky,' indicating experience and confidence, not uncertainty.

C.explanation: The gulls are only one of several signs Ren notices; understanding gull behavior is not his goal or the passage's focus.

D.explanation: The passage shows Ren actively working to protect his plants, implying he believes preparation can help, not that it is futile.

stimulus.text: Young sunflower plants perform a daily motion called heliotropism: their stems bend gradually through the day so that the flower heads face east at dawn, follow the sun as it crosses the sky, then reorient overnight to face east again by the following morning. Once a sunflower matures and begins to bloom heavily, however, this daily rotation stops almost entirely, and the mature flower head remains fixed facing east, tracking the sun no longer.

items.stem: According to the text, what is true of sunflowers?

options.A: Sunflowers face west at dawn and follow the sun until it sets in the east.
options.B: Mature sunflowers track the sun more precisely than young ones do.
options.C: Young sunflowers track the sun across the sky each day, but mature ones no longer do so.
options.D: Sunflowers stop tracking the sun because of cooler autumn temperatures.

items.rationale: The text states young sunflowers follow the sun daily through heliotropism, while mature, heavily blooming sunflowers stop this rotation and stay fixed facing east.

A.explanation: The text states flower heads face east at dawn and follow the sun as it crosses the sky; it does not say they face west at dawn.

B.explanation: The text states mature sunflowers stop tracking the sun almost entirely, the opposite of tracking it more precisely.

D.explanation: The text attributes the stop in tracking to blooming maturity, not to any change in temperature or season.

items.topic: A fictional study of plate colour and appetite

stimulus.text: A researcher hypothesizes that the color of a dinner plate can influence how much food a person serves themselves, with warm colors like red subtly reducing portion sizes by increasing a diner's awareness of the contrast between the food and the plate.

items.stem: Which finding, if true, would most directly support the researcher's hypothesis?

options.A: Diners reported finding red plates more visually appealing than plates of other colors.
options.B: In a cafeteria trial, diners given red plates served themselves 18 percent less pasta, on average, than diners given white plates serving the same dish.
options.C: Diners given red plates ate their meals more quickly than diners given plates of other colors.
options.D: Diners given red plates served themselves the same amount of pasta as diners given white plates.

items.rationale: The hypothesis specifically concerns red plates reducing portion size; a measured, sizable reduction in self-served pasta on red plates compared with white plates directly supports that claim.

A.explanation: Finding a plate visually appealing says nothing about how much food a diner serves, which is what the hypothesis concerns.

C.explanation: Eating speed is a different measure from portion size and is not addressed by the hypothesis.

D.explanation: If portions were the same regardless of plate color, that would undercut, not support, the claim that red plates reduce portion size.

stimulus.text: Historians studying the catalogue of the ancient Kallitheia library, a fictional institution described in surviving trade records, note that its clerks tracked not only a scroll's title and author but its physical condition and its relationship to other works in the collection. Some scholars argue that this catalogue reveals an unusually systematic effort to help future readers locate related material even after an original scroll had been lost or damaged.

items.stem: Which quotation from the catalogue would most directly support the claim that the clerks tried to help future readers find related material even when a scroll was lost?

options.A: 'Scroll 88, a hymn collection, in fair condition, stored on the third shelf from the east wall.'
options.B: 'Scroll 12 was copied twice due to its popularity among visiting scholars.'
options.C: 'Scroll 114, on the grafting of fruit trees, missing since the flood; see scroll 240, which cites its main arguments at length.'
options.D: 'Scroll 301 was removed from the catalogue after its contents were judged inaccurate.'

items.rationale: This entry explicitly notes that a scroll is missing and directs future readers to another scroll preserving its arguments, exactly the kind of cross-referencing the claim describes.

A.explanation: This entry records condition and shelf location, not any connection to a lost scroll or a related text.

B.explanation: This entry notes popularity and copying, which has nothing to do with helping readers find related material after a loss.

D.explanation: Removing an inaccurate scroll from the catalogue does not help readers locate related material; if anything, it reduces the scroll's traceability.

items.topic: Bicycle commuting in four fictional cities

stimulus.text: A transportation study compared bicycle commuting in four fictional cities. Researchers found that greater investment in dedicated bike lanes generally corresponded with a higher share of commuters cycling to work, though the relationship was not perfect: ______

table.caption: Bicycle commuting in four fictional cities

items.stem: Which choice most effectively uses data from the table to complete the text?

options.A: Halmara had both the fewest dedicated bike lanes and the lowest share of bicycle commuters in the study.
options.B: Doria, despite having more dedicated bike lanes than any other city in the study, had a lower share of bicycle commuters than Verinsk.
options.C: Tessaly had more dedicated bike lanes than Halmara but a lower share of bicycle commuters.
options.D: Verinsk had fewer dedicated bike lanes than Doria but a higher share of bicycle commuters, confirming that bike lanes have no effect on commuting rates.

items.rationale: The table shows Doria has the most bike lanes (150 km) of the four cities yet a lower bicycle-commuting share (21%) than Verinsk (34%), exactly the exception to the general pattern the text calls for.

A.explanation: Tessaly, not Halmara, has both the fewest bike lanes (15 km) and the lowest commuting share (8%) in the table.

C.explanation: Tessaly has fewer bike lanes (15 km) than Halmara (40 km), not more, so this reverses the table's values.

D.explanation: The first part of the statement matches the table, but concluding that bike lanes have 'no effect' overstates what a single exception among four data points can establish.

items.topic: Why meteor showers recur each year

stimulus.text: Meteor showers such as the annual display associated with a particular comet's orbit occur when Earth passes through a trail of dust and small debris left behind by that comet on its previous passes near the sun. Because Earth's orbit around the sun is fixed and repeats on a yearly cycle, and because the comet's debris trail remains spread along roughly the same path in space, Earth crosses that trail at nearly the same point in its orbit every year. This suggests that a meteor shower's peak dates from one year to the next would most likely ______.

items.stem: Which choice most logically completes the text?

options.A: shift steadily earlier each year as the comet's orbit gradually decays
options.B: vary widely because the debris trail moves unpredictably through space
options.C: depend mainly on how bright the comet itself appears that year
options.D: fall on nearly the same calendar dates, since Earth reaches the debris trail's location at the same point in its orbit each year

items.rationale: The passage explains that Earth's fixed yearly orbit crosses a debris trail that stays in roughly the same place, so it logically follows that the shower's peak would recur around the same dates each year.

A.explanation: The passage never mentions the comet's orbit decaying or shifting; it describes the debris trail as remaining along roughly the same path.

B.explanation: The passage states the trail 'remains spread along roughly the same path,' which contradicts the idea that it moves unpredictably.

C.explanation: The comet's brightness is never discussed; the passage attributes the shower's timing to Earth's orbit and the trail's fixed position, not brightness.

items.topic: A fictional study of dawn fish-market prices

stimulus.text: Economist Ines Barbosa tracked prices at a coastal fish market where boats arrive at irregular times each dawn, sometimes clustered together and sometimes hours apart. She found that when several boats arrived within the same half hour, prices for common fish fell sharply within minutes of the first sale, but when boats trickled in one at a time across several hours, prices for the same fish stayed high through most of the morning, even though the total volume of fish sold that day was similar in both patterns. Barbosa concludes that buyers set prices less according to the total supply available over a morning than according to ______.

items.stem: Which choice most logically completes the text?

options.A: the reputation of the particular boats that arrive earliest each dawn
options.B: the total volume of fish sold across the entire morning
options.C: how far each boat traveled before reaching the market that morning
options.D: how much fish appears to be available to them at the moment they are deciding what to pay

items.rationale: Barbosa's finding is that prices depend on whether boats cluster together or trickle in, not on total volume, which points to buyers reacting to how much supply seems available right when they are buying.

A.explanation: Boat reputation might plausibly affect prices in general, but the passage never mentions or measures it, so it cannot be the pattern Barbosa's data supports.

B.explanation: The passage states total volume 'was similar in both patterns' even though prices differed, so buyers clearly are not pricing mainly on total volume.

C.explanation: Travel distance is never mentioned in the passage as a factor in the price differences Barbosa observed.

items.topic: Parrotfish producing sand on coral reefs

stimulus.text: Parrotfish spend much of each day scraping algae from coral with their beak-like teeth ______ swallow bits of coral rock along with the algae and grind it into fine sand inside their guts.

items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

options.A: they
options.B: , and they
options.C: , they
options.D: ; and they

items.rationale: The sentence contains two independent clauses; a comma followed by the coordinating conjunction 'and' correctly joins them, giving ', and they.'

A.explanation: Without any punctuation or conjunction, this choice fuses two independent clauses together with no separation.

C.explanation: A comma alone cannot join two independent clauses; this choice lacks the coordinating conjunction needed alongside the comma.

D.explanation: A semicolon should join independent clauses on its own, not be paired with a coordinating conjunction like 'and.'

stimulus.text: Papermakers soak plant fibers such as mulberry bark or cotton rag until they break down into a soft pulp ______ pour the pulp through a mesh screen to drain the water and leave behind a thin, even sheet.

items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

options.A: , and
options.B: ; and
options.C: and
options.D: , they

items.rationale: The subject 'papermakers' governs both 'soak' and 'pour' in a compound predicate, so no comma is needed before the coordinating conjunction 'and.'

A.explanation: A comma is not needed here because 'and' joins two verbs sharing the same subject, not two independent clauses.

B.explanation: A semicolon requires an independent clause on each side, but 'pour the pulp...' shares its subject with the first clause and is not independent.

D.explanation: Adding 'they' creates a second independent clause joined to the first by only a comma, which is a comma splice.

stimulus.text: The rainforest canopy, a dense layer of interlocking branches roughly thirty meters above the ground______supports more species of insects and birds than the shaded forest floor below it.

items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.rationale: The nonessential phrase 'a dense layer of interlocking branches roughly thirty meters above the ground' opens with a comma after 'canopy,' so it must close with a matching comma before 'supports.'

A.explanation: The nonessential element opens with a comma, so closing it with a dash instead creates a mismatched pair of punctuation marks.

C.explanation: A colon cannot be used here because what follows, 'supports more species...,' is not a list or explanation set off from a complete independent clause.

D.explanation: A semicolon requires an independent clause on both sides, but neither the phrase before nor 'supports more species...' alone forms one here.

stimulus.text: Glassblowing studios that specialize in scientific glassware, unlike those that produce decorative pieces______often keep their furnaces burning around the clock, because reheating cold glass from scratch wastes both time and fuel.

items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.rationale: The nonessential phrase 'unlike those that produce decorative pieces' opens with a comma after 'glassware,' so it must close with a matching comma before 'often.'

A.explanation: The nonessential element opens with a comma, so closing it with a dash instead creates a mismatched pair of punctuation marks.

B.explanation: A semicolon requires an independent clause on both sides, but 'often keep their furnaces...' has no subject of its own here.

C.explanation: A colon requires a complete independent clause before it, but the phrase before the blank is an interrupting comparison, not a complete clause.

stimulus.text: Certain desert dunes, when disturbed by wind or by a person's footsteps sliding down their steep faces, ______ a deep, resonant boom that can last up to several minutes and carry for kilometers across open desert.

items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

options.A: produce
options.B: produces
options.C: producing
options.D: had produced

items.rationale: The subject of the verb is the plural noun 'dunes'; despite the intervening singular nouns 'wind,' 'person,' and 'footsteps,' the verb must agree with 'dunes,' so the plural form 'produce' is correct.

B.explanation: This singular verb form wrongly agrees with a nearby singular noun such as 'person' or 'wind' rather than with the true plural subject, 'dunes.'

C.explanation: A nonfinite -ing form cannot serve as the main verb of the sentence, leaving the clause without a complete predicate.

D.explanation: The passage describes a general, ongoing phenomenon in the present tense; the past perfect creates an unsupported shift to an earlier, completed time frame.

stimulus.text: Aluminium is unusual among common metals because recycling it uses only a small fraction of the energy required to refine new metal from ore, which is why municipalities that collect used cans and foil separately from other waste ______ far less energy overall than those that send all metal to a single mixed recycling stream.

items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

options.A: uses
options.B: used
options.C: using
options.D: use

items.rationale: The subject 'municipalities' is plural, and the sentence states a general, present-tense fact, so the plural present-tense verb 'use' is required despite the intervening clause 'that collect used cans and foil separately from other waste.'

A.explanation: This singular verb wrongly agrees with a noun inside the intervening clause rather than with the true plural subject, 'municipalities.'

B.explanation: The sentence states a general, ongoing fact in the present tense elsewhere ('is unusual,' 'uses'), so shifting to the past tense here is inconsistent.

C.explanation: A nonfinite -ing form cannot function as the main verb needed to complete this clause.

stimulus.text: Several species of fungi produce a faint greenish light through a chemical reaction inside ______ cells, a phenomenon that early foresters sometimes mistook for embers smoldering in rotten logs.

items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

options.A: their
options.B: its
options.C: his or her
options.D: they're

items.rationale: The antecedent is 'fungi,' a plural noun, so the plural possessive pronoun 'their' is required.

B.explanation: This singular possessive pronoun does not agree with the plural antecedent 'fungi.'

C.explanation: This pronoun form is used for individual people, not for a plural, non-human antecedent such as 'fungi.'

D.explanation: 'They're' is a contraction of 'they are,' not a possessive form, and does not fit the possessive role needed before 'cells.'

stimulus.text: Originally built from bamboo frames and paper or silk sails, ______ served purposes far beyond recreation, from testing wind currents to signaling across distances too great for a shouting voice to cross.

items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

options.A: the materials
options.B: artisans who built them
options.C: the practice of kite-building
options.D: early kites

items.rationale: The opening phrase 'Originally built from bamboo frames and paper or silk sails' must logically modify the noun that follows it; only 'early kites' were themselves built from those materials.

A.explanation: Materials are not 'built from' materials; the opening phrase cannot logically modify 'the materials' itself.

B.explanation: The artisans were not built from bamboo and sails; they built the objects that were, so this choice misattributes the modifier.

C.explanation: A practice is not a physical object 'built from' bamboo and sails, so it cannot logically follow this opening modifier.

stimulus.text: A solar cooker uses mirrors or reflective panels to concentrate sunlight onto a dark pot, slowly raising the temperature inside enough to cook food without any fuel. ______, solar cookers cannot be used to prepare a meal after sunset or on a heavily overcast day.

items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?

options.A: However
options.B: For example
options.C: Therefore
options.D: Similarly

items.rationale: The first sentence describes a benefit of solar cookers, while the second describes a limitation, so the contrast transition 'However' correctly links the two ideas.

B.explanation: The second sentence is not an instance of the first; it introduces a limitation, not an example of the cooking process just described.

C.explanation: The inability to cook after sunset is not a consequence of how solar cookers work; it is a separate, contrasting limitation.

D.explanation: The two sentences describe a benefit and then a limitation, which are not similar ideas.

stimulus.text: A camel can lose up to a quarter of its body water without suffering the harmful effects that would injure most other mammals long before that point. ______, when a camel finally reaches a water source, it can drink enough in about ten minutes to replace everything it lost.

items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?

options.A: In contrast
options.B: Instead
options.C: Furthermore
options.D: As a result

items.rationale: Both sentences describe remarkable, related abilities camels have regarding water, so the addition transition 'Furthermore' correctly signals that the second fact builds on the first.

A.explanation: The second sentence adds another impressive water-related ability rather than contrasting with the first.

B.explanation: 'Instead' signals a substitution, but the second sentence does not replace or oppose the idea in the first; it adds to it.

D.explanation: The camel's rapid drinking is not caused by its tolerance for water loss; the sentences present two separate, additional facts rather than a cause and effect.

stimulus.text: The Moon's gravity pulls ocean water toward the side of Earth nearest it, creating one high tide there; at the same time, inertia causes water on the far side of Earth to lag behind the planet's pull toward the Moon, creating a second bulge of high water opposite the first. ______, most coastlines experience two high tides and two low tides in roughly a 24-hour period.

items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?

options.A: Consequently
options.B: Nonetheless
options.C: For instance
options.D: Meanwhile

items.rationale: The two water bulges described in the first sentence directly cause the pattern of two daily high tides, so the result transition 'Consequently' correctly links the cause to its effect.

B.explanation: There is no contrast between the two bulges forming and coastlines experiencing two tides; the second follows logically from the first.

C.explanation: The two-tide pattern is not one example among several; it is the direct consequence of the two bulges just described.

D.explanation: 'Meanwhile' signals simultaneous but unrelated events, while the second sentence describes the direct result of the process just explained.

stimulus.text: Some mosaic artists deliberately break new ceramic tiles into irregular fragments rather than purchasing pre-cut mosaic pieces, arguing that uneven edges catch light in ways that uniform pieces cannot. Other artists insist that hand-cutting each fragment slows a project down so much that the technique is impractical for large public installations. ______, many muralists now use a hybrid method, hand-breaking tiles only for a mosaic's focal points and filling the rest of the design with pre-cut pieces.

items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?

options.A: In other words
options.B: As a result
options.C: By contrast
options.D: Similarly

items.rationale: The hybrid method described in the final sentence is a practical response to the tension between the two positions just described, so the result transition 'As a result' correctly links that tension to the compromise solution.

A.explanation: The final sentence does not restate the previous two sentences in different words; it describes a new, third approach that responds to them.

C.explanation: The hybrid method is not simply a contrasting position; it results from and combines elements of the two positions already described.

D.explanation: The hybrid method is a synthesis of two different practices, not a case similar to either one.

stimulus.intro: While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
notes: Bamboo is a grass, not a tree, and some species can grow more than one meter in a single day under ideal conditions.
Unlike trees, bamboo culms (stems) reach their full diameter within weeks and then only grow taller, never thicker.
Rapid growth is possible because bamboo cells are pre-formed in a tightly packed stack inside each new shoot and simply expand with water pressure rather than dividing repeatedly.
Bamboo groves are connected below ground by a shared root system, so a grove can send up dozens of new shoots at once each growing season.
Some farmers harvest bamboo for construction material within three to five years of planting, far sooner than most timber trees.

items.stem: The student wants to explain the specific mechanism that allows bamboo to grow so quickly. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

options.A: Bamboo is a grass rather than a tree, and some farmers harvest it within three to five years of planting.
options.B: Because bamboo groves share a root system, a single grove can send up dozens of shoots in one growing season.
options.C: Bamboo grows quickly because its cells are already stacked inside each new shoot and expand with water pressure instead of dividing repeatedly.
options.D: Bamboo culms reach their full diameter within weeks and then continue growing only in height.

items.rationale: This choice states the precise cellular mechanism the notes give for rapid growth, that pre-formed cells expand with water pressure rather than dividing, directly accomplishing the goal of explaining how bamboo grows so fast.

A.explanation: This combines two true notes but never explains any mechanism behind bamboo's growth rate.

B.explanation: This explains why many shoots can appear at once, a fact about quantity, not the mechanism behind each shoot's rapid growth in height.

D.explanation: This describes a pattern in how diameter and height develop but does not explain the mechanism that makes the growth itself so fast.

stimulus.intro: While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
notes: Snow crystals form when water vapor in a cloud freezes directly onto a tiny dust or pollen particle without first becoming liquid.
The exact six-sided shape of a crystal depends heavily on the temperature and humidity it passes through as it falls.
At temperatures near -2 degrees Celsius, crystals tend to form flat, plate-like shapes; at colder temperatures near -15 degrees Celsius, they tend to form elaborate branching shapes.
Because each crystal follows a slightly different path through the cloud, no two crystals experience the exact same sequence of conditions.
Scientists group snow crystal shapes into categories such as plates, columns, and dendrites to study how they form.

items.stem: The student wants to explain why individual snow crystals rarely look identical to one another. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

options.A: Because each crystal takes a slightly different path through the cloud, no two crystals pass through the exact same sequence of temperature and humidity conditions that shape their growth.
options.B: Snow crystals are classified into categories such as plates, columns, and dendrites to help scientists study their formation.
options.C: Crystals that form near -2 degrees Celsius tend to be flat and plate-like, while those that form near -15 degrees Celsius tend to branch.
options.D: Snow crystals form when water vapor freezes directly onto a dust or pollen particle.

items.rationale: This choice directly links each crystal's unique path through the cloud to the unique sequence of conditions that shapes it, which explains why no two crystals look identical.

B.explanation: This describes how scientists classify shapes for study, which does not explain why individual crystals differ from one another.

C.explanation: This explains how temperature affects general shape categories but does not explain why crystals within similar conditions still vary individually.

D.explanation: This explains how crystals begin forming in general but does not address why individual crystals end up looking different from each other.

stimulus.intro: While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
notes: Leafcutter ants cut fragments of leaves and carry them back to underground nests rather than eating the leaves themselves.
Inside the nest, ants chew the leaf fragments into a pulp and use it to cultivate a specific species of fungus in dedicated garden chambers.
The ants feed on structures the fungus grows specifically in response to being tended, not on the leaves or the fungus's ordinary growth.
Worker ants continuously weed the fungus garden, removing contaminating molds and bacteria that could overwhelm the crop.
A single colony can move several times its own body weight in leaf material in a single night.

items.stem: The student wants to emphasize that leafcutter ants cultivate their food source rather than simply gathering it. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

options.A: A single leafcutter ant colony can carry several times its own body weight in leaves in one night.
options.B: Rather than eating the leaves they collect, leafcutter ants use them to grow a fungus in underground gardens, then feed on structures the fungus produces in response to that care.
options.C: Worker ants weed their fungus gardens to remove molds and bacteria that could destroy the crop.
options.D: Leafcutter ants cut leaf fragments and carry them back to underground nests.

items.rationale: This choice directly contrasts gathering with cultivating, showing that ants convert leaves into a tended fungus crop and eat what that cultivation produces, which precisely accomplishes the stated goal.

A.explanation: This note concerns the quantity of leaves moved, not whether the ants cultivate or merely gather their food.

C.explanation: This shows one part of the cultivation process, garden maintenance, but omits the central point that ants convert leaves into a grown crop rather than eating them directly.

D.explanation: This describes only the gathering step and leaves out the cultivation of fungus that is the point the student wants to emphasize.

stimulus.intro: While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
notes: Engineer Talia Reyes designed a footbridge using a tensioned steel cable deck, which flexes noticeably underfoot but uses roughly 40 percent less steel than a rigid truss design of the same span.
Engineer Dov Amrani designed a rigid truss footbridge for a similar span that costs more in materials but does not sway or bounce, an important feature for a bridge located near a hospital.
Reyes's cable-deck design requires periodic retensioning of the cables every few years to keep the deck level.
Amrani's truss design was assembled off-site in sections and lifted into place in a single day, reducing disruption to traffic below.
Both designs were tested to hold several times the maximum expected pedestrian load before any visible strain appeared.

items.stem: The student wants to explain why an engineer might choose Amrani's design over Reyes's design for a footbridge located near a hospital. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

options.A: Amrani's truss design was assembled off-site and lifted into place in a single day, reducing disruption to traffic below.
options.B: Reyes's design uses roughly 40 percent less steel than a rigid truss design of the same span.
options.C: Amrani's rigid truss design does not sway or bounce, a feature that matters near a hospital, whereas Reyes's cable-deck design flexes noticeably underfoot.
options.D: Both designs were tested to hold several times the maximum expected pedestrian load before showing visible strain.

items.rationale: The notes state directly that Amrani's non-swaying, non-bouncing design is important near a hospital, and contrasting it with Reyes's noticeably flexing deck gives the precise reason to prefer Amrani's design in that location.

A.explanation: Faster, less disruptive assembly is a construction advantage, not a reason tied to the hospital location the student wants to explain.

B.explanation: This is a reason favoring Reyes's design; using it to justify choosing Amrani's design instead reverses what the note actually supports.

D.explanation: This states a similarity between the two designs and does not distinguish why Amrani's design specifically suits a location near a hospital.
